title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The notes construct Teichmüller groupoids S0T_G in genus 0. These are fundamental groupoids of moduli spaces, based not at arbitrary points but at a canonical finite set of 'good' base points. G is a degeneration type (a stable-graph-like datum), and Y is a marked projective line (or the component attached to G).

The previous page singles out marked lines whose automorphism group is large. Typical case: a 'circle structure' Q on the marking set I, i.e. a cyclic order. One embeds Y canonically in P^1 with the marked points on an 'equator' circle, so that the cyclic rotations of I are induced by projective rotations. Rotations act simply transitively on I, so all the tangent circles T_i at the marked points get identified with one another.

In modern terms, T_i is the S^1-torsor of real tangent directions at the point i, and U is the circle group. Taking as axis the direction tangent to the equator gives T_i ≅ U ×_{±1} ω_Q, where ω_Q is the {±1}-torsor of the two orientations of the circle.

This page computes the tangent-direction tori attached to the pieces of a partition of the relevant index set.
- J_I (free marked points): T^Y_{J_I} = U^{J_I} ∧_{±1} ω_Q, with {±1} acting diagonally. There is one global orientation twist.
- J_II (points that come in pairs swapped by an involution σ; these are nodes, i.e. glued half-edges): for each σ-orbit {i, σi}, T_i ⊗ T_{σi} ≅ (U∧ω_Q)⊗(U∧ω_Q) ≅ U canonically, because the two ω_Q twists cancel. Hence T_{J_II} ≅ U^{J_II/σ} is untwisted. Modern reading: the smoothing parameter of a node lives in T_i ⊗ T_j, and a real/equatorial structure trivialises its direction.
- J_III: T_{J_III} ≅ ∏_i U ∧_{±1} E_i, with E_i = ω_Q ∧ J̃_{III,i}. Each E_i is a ±1-torsor combining the orientation with an auxiliary sign torsor J̃_{III,i}.

He then defines E_{G,Q} = E_{Â_1} × ω_Q × E_{J_III}. Here E_{Â_1} = ∏_{a∈Â_1} E_a comes from the other components (presumably by induction). E_{G,Q} is a torsor under the finite elementary abelian 2-group γ_G = {±1}^{Â_1} × {±1} × {±1}^{J_III}.

γ_G maps into U^Â = U^{Â_1} × U^{J_I} × U^{J_II/σ} × U^{J_III}: trivially on the J_II factor, and diagonally on J_I. It therefore embeds in U^{Â_1} × U^{J_I} × U^{J_III}.

The next page concludes:
- the 'SP' torus of tangential data is SP^Y_G ≅ U^Â ∧^{γ_G} E_{G,Q};
- S0T^Q_G is defined as the full subgroupoid of Π_1(SP^Y_G) on the finite set E_{G,Q};
- if J_I = ∅, the ω_Q factor is dropped;
- a presentation by generators and relations is promised.

Purpose. To produce a canonical, symmetric (real, 'equatorial') finite set of tangential base points, equivariant under the automorphisms of the circle structure. These base points are needed to define Teichmüller groupoids in the Esquisse/Lego spirit.
errors: There are no clear mathematical errors.
The left-hand side writes T^Y_{J_II} ≃ U^{J_2}, while the right-hand justification and the later formula show the intended result is U^{J_II/σ} (one circle per σ-orbit). This is a notational slip.

The canonical identification for J_II depends on the two twists ω_Q being literally the same torsor for i and σi. That holds because a single orientation of the equator is used, but it is only sketched (the margin argument is half-legible).
J̃_{III,i} is not defined on this page, so the J_III factor cannot be fully checked.
The struck-out first formula T_{Â_2} = U^A was abandoned.

ideas.what: Unit tangent circles T_i at marked points identified with U ×_{±1} ω_Q via a real/equatorial (cyclic-order) structure, taking the equator tangent as axis.
ideas.modern_name: real tangential base points / tangent directions along the real locus
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1989, tangential base points); Ihara; Brown (dihedral structures on M_{0,n}, 2009)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions base points for Teichmüller groupoids, but not this explicit torsor construction as far as I know

ideas.what: For a node formed by half-edges i, σi, T_i ⊗ T_{σi} is canonically trivial (≅ U) under the circle structure, so node directions carry no sign ambiguity.
ideas.modern_name: trivialization of the smoothing-parameter line T_i⊗T_j at a node over the real locus
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard deformation theory of nodal curves (Deligne–Mumford); real version used in Ihara–Nakamura and Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps

ideas.what: Base point set E_{G,Q} as a torsor under an elementary abelian 2-group γ_G embedded in the torus U^Â, with SP_G = U^Â ∧^{γ_G} E_{G,Q}, and S0T_G the full subgroupoid of Π_1 on E_{G,Q}.
ideas.modern_name: fundamental groupoid with a finite set of (real tangential) base points; Teichmüller groupoid à la Moore–Seiberg / Bakalov–Kirillov / Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (§2-3, Teichmüller tower and base points) in programmatic form only

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a canonical, symmetry-equivariant finite base-point set (a γ_G-torsor of real tangential base points attached to cyclic-order 'equator' structures) for genus-0 Teichmüller groupoids. He announces, but on these pages does not give, a generators-and-relations presentation. The bookkeeping is explicit: orientation torsor ω_Q, the J_I / J_II / J_III split, and cancellation of twists at nodes. It anticipates the later dihedral/real base-point formalisms (Brown's dihedral M_{0,n}, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps) and does not appear in the literature in this form.
missed.quote: on introduit l'ensemble E_{G,Q} = E_{G,Y_Q} = E_{Â_1} × ω_Q × E_{J_III} qui est un torseur sous γ_G = {±1}^{Â_1} × {±1} × {±1}^{J_III}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a historically early, explicit version of the choice of 'good' tangential base points compatible with automorphisms (orbifold points with circle symmetry). This is relevant to GT-actions and to comparisons with Brown's dihedral framework. Even so, the content is likely reconstructible by specialists.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a technically careful but mostly bookkeeping-level construction of torsors of tangential directions. The ideas (real tangential base points, trivial node directions, groupoids on finite base-point sets) are known in later literature, though this explicit equivariant formulation is unpublished and predates them.
transcription_corrections: First line plausibly: '[définie par] Q [comme] équateur, dans le sens des cartes orientées[?]', i.e. a continuation of 'choosing as axis the direction tangent to the equator Q'.
'On aura alors' is correct; the crossed-out formula is 'T_{Â_2} = U^A' (struck).
In 'T^Y_{J_II} ≃ U^{J_2}' the exponent should read J_II (the intended result being U^{J_II/σ}, as on the later line).
Margin under ∧_{i∈J_II}: likely 'mod σ' (product over pairs), not 'somme'.
Margin continuation likely: 'puisque les T_i sont isomorphes chacun à U ∧_{±1} ω_Q, dans le présent contexte, [le produit] de deux d'entre eux ≃ U'.
The group is written γ_{G_?}; the subscript is probably G (as γ_G on the next lines).
'Ǔ^{J_1}' should be read as relating to J_I (likely U^{J_I} or its quotient by the diagonal).
'puisque qui' is probably 'quotient qui' or similar; the last line is 'en factorisant par le produit triple, et on [re]prenant...'.
